land.text: the Oirat core in Dzungaria that Cliopatria draws as the Oirat Confederation (365,737 km2 in 1634)

predecessors.note: The infobox lists '1634: Oirat confederation' as predecessor and the Oirat Confederation page gives 'Disestablished: 1634'. Cliopatria keeps the Oirat Confederation label to 1676 on the same land; this dossier takes the Dzungar Khanate from 1634 (see notes).

land.text: Dzungaria, the Ili country and the Tarim Basin: 'From 1755 to 1758, Qing dynasty took advantage of a Dzungar civil war to conquer Dzungaria'; 'The Tarim Basin was pacified in 1759'; without Hami, which left the state in 1696

successors.note: The infobox gives '1758: Qing dynasty' as successor; this dossier ends the state in 1757, when the last resistance (Amursana, who died of smallpox in Russian lands in September 1757; the Khalkha rebel Chingunjav crushed in 1757) was over. The Tarim Basin went first to the Aq Taghliq khojas' regime (1757) and was pacified by the Qing in 1759 (Dzungar page); Hami left the Dzungar state in 1696.

capitals.name: Khobak Sari (Ghulja, Yining)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Ghulja'; body: 'He also established Ghulja as the capital city, naming it Khobak Sari' (of Erdeni Batur, reign 1634-1653; the page gives no year). The end year is the Qing campaign of 1755 that reached the Ili; the page names no earlier or later seat.

rulers.name: Sengge
rulers.note: Infobox '1653-1671'; the page has the coup of Chechen Tayiji and Zotov against him and his assassination in 1670, and the Galdan page 'Sengge solidified his rule in 1661'.

rulers.name: Galdan Boshugtu Khan
rulers.note: Infobox '1671-1697'; the Dalai Lama gave him the title Boshogtu Khan in 1678 or 1679 (Dzungar page 1678, Galdan page 1679); he died in 1697 (the Galdan page: poison on 4 April in the text, 3 May in the infobox).

rulers.name: Galdan Tseren
rulers.note: Infobox '1727-1745'; the page has him dying in 1745.

rulers.name: Tsewang Dorji Namjal
rulers.note: Infobox '1746-1750'; the body says Lama Dorji seized the throne from his younger brother in 1749, so the infobox dates conflict with the text.

rulers.name: Dawachi
rulers.note: Infobox '1753-1755 (last)'; the Qing 'forced Dawachi to surrender' in 1755 (Dzungar-Qing Wars page).

correction.text: unchanged shape, reassigned to oirat-confederation: no Dzungar state exists before 1634 (infobox 'Established: 1634')

keyframe_review.note: 365,737 km2 for 1609-1618 (79.9-91.0 E, 42.2-49.6 N: Dzungaria). The page has 'Established: 1634' and 'About 1620 the western Mongols, known as the Oirats, united in the Junggar Basin in Dzungaria'; there was no Dzungar Khanate in these years. The land is the Oirat core, which Cliopatria draws again from 1619 as the Oirat Confederation (identical area, 365,737 km2); the oirat-confederation dossier draws it from 1609 (page: 'From 1609-1616, the Oirats devastated the Kazakhs and the Kyrgyz').

correction.text: the Dzungarian core on the upper Emil and Ili rivers and the Junggar basin, 365,737 km2

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1634-1657: the 365,737 km2 Dzungarian core (Cliopatria's Oirat Confederation shape of 1619-1635). Cliopatria enlarges the Oirat row to 839,091 km2 in 1636, but the pages show only raids and fighting for Semirechye in these years (1635 Jangir captured, winter 1643 and 1645-46 campaigns, 1652 Jangir killed) and the border consolidated 'from the Ayagoz River to the Talas River' only after the Chu and Talas victory of 1658. Infobox area '1650: 3,600,000 km2' is 4.3 times the 839,091 km2 shape of that year; it equals Cliopatria's 1687-1695 peak (3.65 M km2), so the infobox year is probably wrong rather than the shape. Re-checked 2026-10-19 on the Erdeni Batur page: 1635 'invaded the Kazakh Khanate, and captured Jangir Khan at the Ili river'; 1646 'capturing Sairam and Turkistan', but 'soon Bukharans relieved the captured cities'; the page is silent on Jetisu and on 1636, so the core shape still stands to 1657.

correction.text: Dzungaria and eastern Semirechye from the Ayagoz River to the Talas River, 838,700 km2

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1658-1676: Cliopatria's 839,091 km2 shape (its Oirat Confederation rows of 1636-1676), applied from 1658 when 'The border was consolidated from the Ayagoz River to the Talas River' after the Dzungar victory on the Chu and Talas rivers. No page opened dates the Tarim, Turfan or Hami holdings before 1678-1680, so none is in this shape.

correction.text: unchanged shape, years 1677-1678 only (the Tarim Basin is added in 1680)

keyframe_review.note: 839,091 km2 for 1677-1682 (73.4-91.0 E, 38.5-49.6 N): the same shape as the Oirat rows. It holds for 1677-1678 only; the Tarim Basin and Turfan-Hami are added from 1679-1680 (new keyframe dzungar-khanate_1680), three years before Cliopatria's 1683 shape. The victory over Ochirtu 'in 1677' (Galdan page: 1678) changes no outline. No ledger gain: the Ochirtu victory moves no land (wars/2); the Oirat pastures are inside the 1658 keyframe.

correction.text: the Dzungar lands of 1677 with Altishahr (the Tarim Basin) and Turpan-Hami

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1680-1682: the 1677 shape plus the Tarim Basin ('Conquest of Altishahr: 1680-1681'; 'Galdan led 30,000 men to Turpan and Hami' in 1679, Galdan page 'the next year' after 1681, i.e. 1682). Cliopatria's 1683 shape (1.72 M km2) carries both.

1.72 M km2 for 1683-1686 (69.7-95.9 E, 36.6-49.6 N): Dzungaria, Semirechye, the Tarim Basin and Turfan-Hami, reaching 69.7 E at the Fergana and Syr Darya edge. Right for the Tarim and Hami; the Kyrgyz were 'subjugated' and the Fergana Valley 'devastated' in campaigns from 1683 to 1685 and the Syr Darya cities held 1684-1687 (ledger), not annexed Fergana. Years start three years early for the Tarim (1680). Revised 2026-11-01 (fx-25): verdict ok -> adjust. Cliopatria's 1683 shape (5,921 cells) lacks about 1,180 Tarim Basin cells that ledger 4-5 give to the Dzungars in 1679-1680 and that keyframe dzungar-khanate_1680 (6,758 cells) draws, so the 1683 check removed them and the 1687 check then re-added them as part of a 6,468-cell snap. Galdan page (opened 2026-11-01): 'The Dzungars conquered Kashgar and Yarkant', 'He conquered Turfan and Hami the next year', 'The Dzungars kept control over the Tarim Basin until 1757'. The corrected shape is the 1683 shape with the Tarim Basin and Turfan-Hami regions, as in the 1680 keyframe.

union.text: Dzungaria, Semirechye and the Syr Darya edge as Cliopatria draws them in 1683
Altishahr (Kashgar and Yarkant), held by the Dzungars from 1680

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1683 shape plus the Tarim Basin and Turpan-Hami that the ledger holds from 1679-1680 (the 1683 shape leaves out about 1,180 Tarim cells)

union.text: Dzungaria, Semirechye and the Syr Darya edge as Cliopatria draws them in 1683
Altishahr (Kashgar and Yarkant), held by the Dzungars from 1680

correction.text: the Dzungar lands of 1683 with the Tarim Basin, Turpan-Hami and Outer Mongolia (Khalkha), years 1688-1690

keyframe_review.note: 3.65 M km2 for 1687-1690 (73.4-109.0 E, 35.4-53.6 N): adds all Outer Mongolia (Khalkha). The shape holds from August 1688, not 1687: 'Galdan entered Khalkha territory in 1688' (battle of Olgoi Lake on 3 August 1688); 1687 is the trigger (the killing of Dorjijab). The 53.6 N edge reaches beyond the lands the pages name (Khalkha and the Khangai-Altai), so the north is soft. Infobox '1650: 3.6 M km2' agrees with this peak. Revised 2026-11-01 (fx-25): the keyframe now starts in 1688, as its own text says (it started in 1687 and snapped the ledger by 6,468 cells before Galdan reached Khalkha). Shape changed from Cliopatria's 1687 outline to the 1683 shape with Tarim Basin, Turfan-Hami and all Outer Mongolia, which is what the ledger holds (ledger 4, 5 and 8). Galdan page (opened 2026-11-01): 'he entered Khalkha territory in 1688', 'fought with them near Olgoi Lake on August 3, 1688. The Oirats won after a 3-day battle'. The rest of Cliopatria's 1687 outline (Tuva 571 cells, Pamir and Qinghai edges, Alxa and Ordos in Inner Mongolia held by the Qing) is dropped: the page does not mention Tuva, the Uriankhai, Gansu or the Yenisei Kyrgyz, and no other page opened names them.

union.text: Dzungaria, Semirechye and the Syr Darya edge as Cliopatria draws them in 1683
Altishahr (Kashgar and Yarkant), held by the Dzungars from 1680
Khalkha Mongolia, drawn contested with the Qing 1690-1696

correction.text: the 1688-1690 outline carried forward; Outer Mongolia (Khalkha) drawn contested between the Dzungars and the Qing, 1690-1696

keyframe_review.note: 3.65 M km2 for 1691-1695, same outline. The Dzungar-Qing page: 'Galdan was left in control of Mongolia' after Ulan Butung (September 1690) while 'The Khalkha rulers declared themselves Qing vassals at Dolon Nor' in 1691; the Dzungar page: 'In 1696, Galdan was defeated by the Qing dynasty and lost Outer Mongolia'. The shape stays but Outer Mongolia is the contested zone 1690-1696 (blend with the Qing), not plain Dzungar land. Revised 2026-11-01 (fx-25): the outline is the same corrected outline as the 1688 keyframe (1683 shape with Tarim Basin, Turfan-Hami and Outer Mongolia), not Cliopatria's 1691 shape, so the 1691 check does not re-add the Tuva and Inner Mongolia margins that the 1688 keyframe drops.

2.05 M km2 for 1696-1708: Outer Mongolia is gone after Zuunmod/Jao Modo (12 June 1696 on the Galdan page, May 1696 on the Dzungar-Qing page). Dzungaria, Semirechye, the Tarim Basin and Turfan-Hami remain. Hami goes the same year: 'Abdullah Tarkhan Beg of Hami also rebelled in 1696 and defected to the Qing dynasty'; 'In 1698, Qing troops were stationed in Hami' (ledger 1696). The shape is corrected to lose Hami (a 220 km radius round Hami removes about 122,000 km2 by the gazetteer's cell count, the eastern tip of Cliopatria's shape to 95.9 E). Dzungaria, Semirechye, the Tarim Basin and Turpan remain.

correction.text: the 1696-1708 shape without Hami (Qomul) and the oasis lands east of Turpan, which defected to the Qing in 1696

keyframe_review.note: 2.05 M km2 for 1709-1717, no change of outline. Events of the years (Tsewang Rabtan's war on the Qing, sack of Hami in 1714, Kazakh invasion of 1708 repelled 1711-1712) move no frontier on the pages. Hami is outside the shape from 1696 (ledger): 'sacking Hami' in 1714 is a raid on a Qing-held oasis, and no page has the Dzungars holding it again.

correction.text: the 1709-1717 shape without Hami (Qomul) and the oasis lands east of Turpan, which defected to the Qing in 1696
the 1718-1720 shape, December 1717-1720, with Central Tibet held by a Dzungar military government, without Hami (Qomul) and the oasis lands east of Turpan, which defected to the Qing in 1696

keyframe_review.note: 2.69 M km2 for 1718-1720 (73.4-96.2 E, 28.9-49.6 N): adds Tibet. The Tibet page has the Dzungars through the Largin pass on 25 August 1717, Lhasa taken and Lha-bzang Khan dead on 2 December 1717, a 'military government' and an occupation 'from 1717 to 1720', so the shape holds from December 1717 and ends with the Qing expulsion in 1720. The page does not say how far the occupation reached (Ue-Tsang or Kham), so the Tibetan part is soft. Hami is removed as in 1696. Re-checked 2026-10-19 on the Chinese expedition to Tibet (1720) page: it is silent on how far the occupation reached, so the Tibetan part stays soft.

2.05 M km2 for 1721-1726: Tibet is lost in 1720. The Dzungar invasion of 'the oases of Central Asia in 1723' takes Tashkent and Turkistan from the Kazakhs outside this shape; the ledger carries it as an occupation (hatched) to 1745. Hami is removed as in 1696.

correction.text: the 1721-1726 shape without Hami (Qomul) and the oasis lands east of Turpan, which defected to the Qing in 1696

keyframe_review.note: 2.05 M km2 for 1727-1751. The page has Hami and Turpan tension (Turpan 'had previously defected to the Qing dynasty', attacked in 1731), the 1739 boundary with Khalkha, and the Tarim rebellion after Galdan Tseren's death in 1745; none redraws the outline, apart from Hami, which is removed from 1696 (ledger). Turpan stays: the Dzungar page says only that a local chief, Emin Khoja, 'defected to the Qing dynasty' (after the 1720 Tibet campaign, no year) and that in 1731 the Dzungars attacked it; the Turpan page (read 2026-10-19) is silent on any Qing submission, so no loss is dated.

correction.text: the 1727-1751 shape without Hami (Qomul) and the oasis lands east of Turpan, which defected to the Qing in 1696
the 1752-1756 shape without Hami (Qomul) and the oasis lands east of Turpan, which defected to the Qing in 1696; plain Dzungar land 1752-1754, contested with the Qing 1755-1757

keyframe_review.note: 2.05 M km2 for 1752-1756. Right to 1754; the Qing army was sent 'in the spring of 1755', surprised Dawachi 'at the site of Borotola in June 1755' and 'destroyed the Dzungar Khanate within the span of 100 days'; Amursana's revolt and Qing-Kazakh fighting ran to mid-1757. The shape is kept for 1755-1757 but drawn contested with the Qing (ledger 1755-1757). Hami is removed as in 1696.

correction.text: the 1752-1756 shape without Hami (lost in 1696), in its last year, held by the last resistance and contested with the Qing

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1757: Cliopatria ends the Dzungar row in 1756, but the Dzungar genocide page dates the campaign 1755-1758, with the Khalkha rebel Chingunjav 'crushed in 1757' and 'The Dzungars kept control over the Tarim Basin until 1757' (Galdan page). The last year of the state uses the 1752 shape, contested. Hami is removed as in 1696. From 1757 the Tarim Basin is held by the Aq Taghliq khojas' regime (ledger 1757), pacified by the Qing in 1759.

region.text: the upper Emil River south of the Tarbagatai Mountains, with Dzungaria

ledger.note: 1634: Erdeni Batur founds the Dzungar Khanate on the upper Emil River. The infobox gives 'Established: 1634'; 'was sent back to establish the Dzungar Khanate on the upper Emil River south of the Tarbagatai Mountains'; 'About 1620 the western Mongols, known as the Oirats, united in the Junggar Basin in Dzungaria.' The Oirat Confederation page has 'Disestablished: 1634'.

region.text: Kazakh lands east of the Talas: the pass of Orbulaq and the lands of Jangir's Kazakhs

ledger.note: 1643: Erdeni Batur's army enters Kazakh lands. 'In the winter of 1643, the Oirats launched a campaign into Kazakhstan'; the Kazakh-Dzungar Wars page has the battle of Orbulaq (600 Kazakhs against 50,000 Dzungars in a pass) and a relief army from the Samarkand emir; further campaigns 1645-46. Earlier: 'The Dzungars invaded the Kazakh Khanate in 1635, capturing their sultan' Jangir (no ground held).

region.text: the border country between the Ayagoz River and the Talas River

ledger.note: 1658: the Kazakh frontier is fixed. 'A Dzungar force defeated a Bukharan relief force on the Chu and Talas rivers'; 'The border was consolidated from the Ayagoz River to the Talas River.' Jangir had been killed in his third major battle with the Dzungars in 1652.

region.text: Semirechye between the Ayagoz River and the Talas River

ledger.note: 1658: eastern Semirechye passes to the Dzungars. 'The border was consolidated from the Ayagoz River to the Talas River' after the victory on the Chu and Talas rivers. The kazakh-khanate dossier has the matching loss, dated 1658, under the counterpart name oirat-confederation.

region.text: Turpan and Hami

ledger.note: 1679: Galdan takes Turpan and Hami. 'In 1679, Galdan led 30,000 men to Turpan and Hami'; the Galdan page says only 'He conquered Turfan and Hami the next year' (after the 1681 Kazakh campaign, so about 1682). The page does not say who held the oases, so the counterpart is the oasis rulers.

region.text: Altishahr: Kashgar and Yarkant and the Tarim Basin

ledger.note: 1680: the Dzungars conquer the Tarim Basin. 'Conquest of Altishahr: 1680-1681'; 'soon in 1680, Galdan led 120,000 men into the Yarkent Khanate and conquered it'; 'Between 1680 and 1688, the Dzungars conquered the Tarim Basin'; Galdan page: 'The Dzungars conquered Kashgar and Yarkant', client ruler Afaq installed after the Black Mountain Khoja was overthrown (request of 1677); 'The Dzungars kept control over the Tarim Basin until 1757.' Another sentence of the Dzungar page has Yarkand captured in 1678.

region.text: Sayram, Shymkent and Tashkent on the Syr Darya

ledger.note: 1684: the Syr Darya cities fall to Galdan. 'Tsewang Rabtan took Sayram and left a garrison. Civilians revolted, and Galdan retook the city. Galdan then took nine Syr Darya cities, including Sayram and Shymkent. Tashkent surrendered voluntarily.' (Sieges of Sayram failed in 1681 and 1683.) The year of the nine cities follows the page's 1684 entry.

region.text: Sayram, Shymkent and Tashkent on the Syr Darya

ledger.note: 1687: Tauke Khan drives Galdan out. 'Per Russian reports, Tauke Khan, with 10,000 Bukharan troops, drove Galdan from Kazakh lands'; 1688: Tauke Khan recaptured Tashkent. (Galdan page: he besieged Turkistan in 1687 without taking it.)

region.text: Khalkha Mongolia

ledger.note: August 1688: Galdan conquers Khalkha Mongolia. 'Galdan entered Khalkha territory in 1688'; 'At the Olgoi Lake battle on August 3, 1688, The Oirats won after a 3-day battle'; Zanabazar and Chakhundorji submitted to the Qing in September. Dzungar page: 'Galdan led 30,000 Dzungar troops into Khalkha Mongolia in 1688'.

region.text: Khalkha Mongolia, left to Galdan after Ulan Butung but claimed by the Qing

ledger.note: September 1690: the Qing meet Galdan at Ulan Butung. 'the Qing finally confronted the Dzungars at Ulan Butung in September 1690'; the Dzungars escaped, 'Galdan was left in control of Mongolia'; 'The Khalkha rulers declared themselves Qing vassals at Dolon Nor' in 1691. Dzungar page: Galdan crossed the Kherlen River with 20,000 late in the summer of 1690.

region.text: Hami (Qomul) and the oasis lands east of Turpan, the eastern tip of the Dzungar shape (93.9-95.9 E)

ledger.note: 1696: Hami leaves the Dzungar state. 'Abdullah Tarkhan Beg of Hami also rebelled in 1696 and defected to the Qing dynasty.' 'In 1698, Qing troops were stationed in Hami.' The page gives no month. The 220 km radius is the eastern tip of Cliopatria's 1696-1756 shape (to 95.9 E), which is my reading of the oasis lands; no page gives the extent. Hami is not drawn as Dzungar again: the page has Tsewang Rabtan 'sacking Hami' in 1714, a raid, and names no later Dzungar hold. Turpan stays Dzungar because the page dates its defection to no year (see notes).

region.text: Khalkha Mongolia

ledger.note: June 1696: Galdan is routed at Zuunmod. 'On 12 June 1696, the same day Kangxi turned back, Galdan blundered into the western army.' (Dzungar-Qing page: 'the Battle of Jao Modo in May 1696', which 'broke the Dzungar army as a military force'.)

region.text: Outer Mongolia (Khalkha)

ledger.note: 1696: Outer Mongolia goes to the Qing. 'In 1696, Galdan was defeated by the Qing dynasty and lost Outer Mongolia.' Dzungar-Qing page: after 1697 'Khalkha Mongolia was placed under Qing rule, with a garrison near present-day Ulaanbaatar'; Galdan died in 1697.

region.text: Tibet: Lhasa and the Khoshut lands of Lha-bzang Khan

ledger.note: August 1717: the Dzungars enter Tibet. 'On August 25, 1717' they passed the Largin pass; Lhasa was reached by 8 October. The khoshut-khanate dossier has the same contest.

region.text: Lhasa and Central Tibet

ledger.note: December 1717: Lha-bzang Khan dies at the Potala. 'December 2, 1717, when the Potala Palace was attacked'; Tseren Dhondup attacked Lhasa on 30 November 1717 and 'looted monasteries and massacred the city's population'.

region.text: Lhasa and Ue-Tsang under a Dzungar military government (Tibetan land, hatched)

ledger.note: December 1717: the Dzungars occupy Central Tibet. 'The Dzungar conquest was short-lived with about the occupation of the region lasting from 1717 to 1720'; 'the Dzungars established a military government in the region and influenced the Tibetan military'; Lhasa fell after 'December 2nd of 1717, Potala Palace was attacked'. The page speaks of occupation and a military government and never of annexation, so the land stays Tibet's (tibet dossier, ledger/19 records the same occupation with the roles reversed) and is drawn hatched. The page does not say how far the occupation reached beyond Lhasa; Central Tibet is the reading. fx-54 (3 Nov 2026): was a plain gain from khoshut-khanate, which drew Central Tibet as Dzungar land.

region.text: Tibet, expelled in 1720

ledger.note: 1720: the Qing drive the Dzungars out of Tibet and the occupation ends. 'In 1720, the Qing dynasty sent a large force under the leadership of Prince Xun, Yunti'; 'The larger expedition expelled the Dzungars and directly led to the Qing rule of Tibet, up until the Xinhai Revolution'. (An earlier Qing relief force was destroyed at the Salween River in 1718.) fx-54 (3 Nov 2026): was a loss to qing-dynasty, which handed Central Tibet to the Qing as if it had been Dzungar land; the tint of the Qing protectorate belongs to the qing-dynasty dossier.

region.text: Tashkent, Sayram-Shymkent and Turkistan, the Dzungar hold on the Syr Darya cities and Jetisu

ledger.note: 1723: the Dzungars take the Syr Darya cities. 'Lobsangsur's force of 30,000+ defeated the Kazakhs at Sayram, Tashkent, and Khara-Murut. The Dzungars captured Turkistan'. Dzungar page: 'launched their largest attack on the oases of Central Asia in 1723'; 'The Dzungars controlled Jetisu and Tashkent until 1745.' Hatched, not annexed. Fergana: the Kazakh-Dzungar Wars page also says 'They also captured Khujand, Samarkand, and Andijan, occupying the Fergana Valley', its only sentence on those places, with no end date. The Khanate of Kokand page (read 2026-10-19) has no Dzungar hold in 1723: it dates the Dzungar invasion of Tashkent and Kokand to 1742 ('a 30,000-strong Dzungar army ... stalled due to fierce resistance'), the invasion of the Fergana Valley and the siege of Kokand to 1745, and 'a full Dzungar withdrawal' after Galdan Tseren's death in September 1745. A Fergana occupation of 1723-1745 is therefore not drawn: no page gives it a dated start and end, and the two pages do not agree. The zone stays Tashkent, Sayram-Shymkent and Turkistan.

region.text: the Khovd and Altai country between Khalkha and Dzungaria (Khoton Lake, Erdene Zuu)

ledger.note: 1731: the Qing invade, the Dzungars win at Khoton Lake. 'sent an invasion force of 10,000 in the early 1730s, which the Dzungars defeated near the Khoton Lake'; 'In 1731, the Dzungars attacked Turpan, which had previously defected to the Qing dynasty'; the Khalkhas defeated the Dzungars near Erdene Zuu in 1732. The fighting is in the Altai country between Khalkha and Dzungaria.

region.text: the Khalkha-Dzungar boundary of 1739

ledger.note: 1739: the Khalkha-Dzungar boundary is agreed. 'In 1739, Galdan Tseren agreed to the boundary between Khalkha and Dzungar territory'; the Dzungar-Qing page: the Qing 'made peace with the Dzungar Khanate' and 'decided the border between them in a 1739 treaty'.

region.text: Tashkent, Sayram-Shymkent and Turkistan, the Dzungar hold on the Syr Darya cities and Jetisu

ledger.note: 1745: the Dzungar hold on Jetisu and Tashkent ends. 'The Dzungars controlled Jetisu and Tashkent until 1745'; Galdan Tseren died in 1745, 'triggering widespread rebellion in the Tarim Basin' (Kazakh-Dzungar Wars page: civil war and the Kazakh Ablai seizing herds and territory). Conflict on the Kazakh-Dzungar Wars page: a 1734 Russian report says the Senior Jus khan 'had taken possession of the former cities of Tashkent and others', 'which had previously been conquered by the former Dzungar ruler, the khongtaiji', 'but which his son Galdan Tseren had abandoned because of the war with China'; a second 1734 account on the same page dates a change in the control of Tashkent, Turkestan and Sairam to 'fifteen years ago' (bracketed 'apparently five years ago'), and the page gives no single date for the Dzungar withdrawal. The hold may have ended in the 1730s; 1745 is the Dzungar page's year, so confidence is 2.

region.text: Dzungaria and the Ili country (Ghulja)

ledger.note: Spring 1755: the Qing army enters the Dzungar lands. 'In the spring of 1755, the Qianlong Emperor dispatched an army'; the Qing surprised Dawachi 'at the site of Borotola in June 1755'; 'The Qing army met almost no resistance and destroyed the Dzungar Khanate within the span of 100 days.' Dzungar-Qing page: Zhaohui's forces 'forced Dawachi to surrender'. Amursana, made Khoit khan, rebelled (genocide page).

region.text: Dzungaria and the Ili country

ledger.note: 1757: the last resistance ends. Amursana 'died of smallpox in Russian lands in September 1757' (Dzungar page); the Khalkha prince Chingunjav, who rebelled in 1756, was 'crushed in 1757' and executed; 'The Qing campaign reached its peak' in 1757-1758.

region.text: the Tarim Basin held by the Dzungars until 1757

ledger.note: 1757: the Dzungar hold on the Tarim Basin ends. 'The Dzungars kept control over the Tarim Basin until 1757.' (Galdan page.) The land does not pass to the Qing in 1757. Dzungar page: 'When Amursana rebelled against the Qing dynasty, the Aq Taghliq (i.e., "White Mountaineers", also known as Afaqis) Khojas Burhanuddin and Jahan rebelled in Yarkand' (no year given for the rebellion); 'In February 1758, the Qing sent Yaerhashan and Zhao Hui with 10,000 troops against the Aq Taghliq regime'; Zhao Hui was 'besieged ... at Yarkand until January 1759'; 'The Tarim Basin was pacified in 1759.' So the counterpart is the khojas' regime and the Qing gain is 1759 (for the qing-dynasty dossier). The counterpart is a string: no dossier exists for the khojas' regime (listed as needed).

region.text: Dzungaria and the Ili country

ledger.note: 1757: Dzungaria goes to the Qing. 'From 1755 to 1758, Qing dynasty took advantage of a Dzungar civil war to conquer Dzungaria and wipe out the Dzungar people' (Dzungar page); the genocide page puts 70-80 percent of the Dzungar population dead (420,000-800,000) and settles Han, Hui, Uyghur, Sibe and Manchu colonists on state farms in Dzungaria from 1760.

region.text: Dzungaria, the Ili country and the Tarim Basin (the 1756 shape without Hami, lost in 1696)

ledger.note: 1757: the Dzungar Khanate is no more. The infobox succession entry reads '1758: Qing dynasty'; 'The Qing army ... destroyed the Dzungar Khanate within the span of 100 days' (1755); the last resistance ends in 1757. Dzungaria passes to the Qing (identity.successors); the Tarim Basin passes first to the Aq Taghliq khojas (ledger 1757) and to the Qing in 1759; Cliopatria's last Dzungar year is 1756.

wars.name: Kazakh-Dzungar Wars

zones.text: eastern Semirechye, fixed 1658 from the Ayagoz to the Talas
the Syr Darya cities taken 1684-87 and 1723-45

wars.outcome: Dzungar gains in Semirechye (1658) and on the Syr Darya (1684-87, 1723-1745); the Kazakhs won at Bulanty (1726) and in 1727-1730; the last war ended in May 1741, with Dzungar hostages from the Middle Jus in 1742.
wars.note: Infobox 'Date: 1635-1742'. The Dzungar page extends the fighting to 1752-1755 (final clashes with the Middle Jus).

wars.name: Dzungar conquest of the Tarim Basin
wars.outcome: Galdan conquers Kashgar and Yarkant (1680), installs a client and holds the Tarim Basin to 1757.
wars.note: The Dzungar page has Yarkand captured in 1678 and the conquest in 1680-1681; the Black Kyrgyz raided Moghulistan in 1680.

wars.name: Khoshut-Dzungar war (Galdan against Ochirtu)
wars.outcome: Galdan defeats Chechen Tayiji near Sayram Lake (1676) and Ochirtu (1677 on the Dzungar page, 1678 on the Galdan page); Ochirtu flees to Kokonor and Galdan dominates the Oirats.
wars.note: Ochirtu's defeat is 1677 on the Dzungar page ('The victory over Ochirtu in 1677 resulted in Galdan's domination of the Oirats') and 1678 on the Galdan page ('In 1678 Galdan forced Ochirtu to flee to Kokonur and established hegemony over the Oirats'). No frontier moved, so there is no ledger gain and no zone: the Oirat pastures of Ochirtu's Khoshuts lie inside the dzungar-khanate_1658 keyframe (839,091 km2, drawn 1658-1676), and khoshut-khanate (Qinghai and Tibet) never held Dzungaria and has no 1677 loss. A 1677 gain 'from khoshut-khanate' was removed after review (2026-10-19).

wars.name: First Dzungar-Qing War
wars.outcome: Galdan wins at Olgoi Nor (3 Aug 1688), meets the Qing at Ulan Butung (Sept 1690), is routed at Zuunmod (12 June 1696) and dies in 1697; Outer Mongolia passes to the Qing.
wars.note: The Dzungar-Qing Wars page dates the war 1687-1697; Khalkha rulers declared themselves Qing vassals at Dolon Nor in 1691. Hami's ruler Abdullah Tarkhan Beg rebelled and defected to the Qing in 1696 (ledger 1696), part of the same war but not a Khalkha zone.

wars.name: Dzungar conquest of Tibet
wars.outcome: Tsewang Rabtan's army enters Tibet (25 Aug 1717), kills Lha-bzang Khan (2 Dec 1717), destroys a Qing relief force at the Salween River (1718) and is expelled by the Qing in 1720.
wars.note: The infobox dates the campaign 1716-1720 and the result as a Dzungar victory.

wars.name: Third Dzungar-Qing War

zones.text: the Altai frontier between Khalkha and Dzungaria

wars.outcome: Dzungar victory at Khoton Lake (1731), Khalkha victory at Erdene Zuu (1732); peace and a fixed boundary in 1739.
wars.note: The Dzungar page lists a 'second Qing war (1715-1720)' with the sack of Hami in 1714, the Qing Salween defeat of 1718 and the 1720 Tibet campaign.

wars.name: Dzungar-Kokand clashes
wars.outcome: 'The Dzungars invaded Kokand in 1742 and 1745 and were repelled'; no frontier moved.

wars.name: Qing conquest of Dzungaria
wars.outcome: Qing victory: the khanate destroyed in 1755, Amursana's revolt and the Dzungar genocide 1755-1758, the Tarim Basin pacified in 1759.

certainty.note: Steppe and oasis frontiers; the Kazakh border 'from the Ayagoz River to the Talas River' (1658) is described by its rivers only.
The Khalkha-Dzungar boundary is agreed in 1739 and so firmer there; every other frontier stays soft.

notes:
Cliopatria rows reviewed: Dzungar Khanate (1609-1756, 11 shapes). The dossier starts the state in 1634 ('Established: 1634' on the Dzungar page; the Oirat page: 'Disestablished: 1634'), not in 1609 or 1677 as Cliopatria's two rows imply. Cliopatria draws one continuous realm under three labels: 'Dzungar Khanate' 1609-1618, 'Oirat Confederation' 1619-1676 (shapes of identical area, 365,737 then 839,091 km2) and 'Dzungar Khanate' again from 1677. This dossier gives 1609-1633 to oirat-confederation and takes the Oirat rows of 1634-1676 as new keyframes (dzungar-khanate_1634 and _1658); the oirat-confederation dossier marks those Oirat shapes wrong for its own years. CONSEQUENCE FOR OTHER DOSSIERS: the kazakh-khanate ledger (1643 contest_start, 1658 contest_end and loss) names oirat-confederation as counterpart; with this split the counterpart for those three events should read dzungar-khanate. If the colour agent prefers one colour for the whole realm, the alternative is to merge oirat-confederation (1609-1634) into this dossier.

Area check: infobox '1650: 3,600,000 km2' against Cliopatria 839,091 km2 for 1650 (ratio 0.23). It matches Cliopatria's peak of 3.65 M km2 in 1687-1695 (Galdan's Mongolia), so the infobox year is probably wrong; the shape stands. The page's undated 'Total: 4.56 km2' is a typo.

Unresolved (page silent): (1) Hami: the Dzungar page dates its loss ('Abdullah Tarkhan Beg of Hami also rebelled in 1696 and defected to the Qing dynasty'; 'In 1698, Qing troops were stationed in Hami'), so the ledger has a 1696 loss to the Qing and the shapes from 1696 are corrected minus Hami (220 km radius, my reading of the extent); the Dzungars 'sacked Hami' in 1714, a raid. Turpan: the page says only that it 'had previously defected to the Qing dynasty' before the 1731 attack, after the Dzungars left Tibet in 1720; no year, and the Turpan page is silent, so Turpan stays in the shapes (gap). (2) The 1636 enlargement of the Oirat row to Semirechye is not on any page; this dossier keeps the 365,737 km2 core to 1657. (3) Tibet: extent of the 1717-1720 occupation. (4) Turfan-Hami capture year: 1679 (Dzungar page) against about 1682 (Galdan page). (5) Yarkand captured 1678 or 1680. (6) Ochirtu's defeat 1677 (Dzungar) or 1678 (Galdan); Galdan's death 4 April (Galdan page text) or 3 May 1697 (its infobox). (7) Month of Zuunmod: 12 June 1696 (Galdan page) or May 1696 (Dzungar-Qing page). (8) The page gives no year for Ghulja as capital.

The Yarkent Khanate of Kashgaria (to 1680) is the eastern-moghulistan dossier, whose 1680 loss to this state mirrors /ledger/6 (counterpart corrected from yarkent-khanate by the ia-03-d reviewer, 2026-10-19). Counterparts without dossiers (names used as strings): Khalkha Mongols (the three Khalkha khanates, no Cliopatria row after the Mongol Khanate ends in 1635); Turfan and Hami oasis rulers (the Kumul Khanate is the likely state, not named by the pages); the Aq Taghliq (Afaqi) khojas' regime of Yarkand (1757-1759, counterpart of the Tarim loss). Gazetteer: Sayram has no place entry (Shymkent used, 12 km away); native names are standard Mongolian and Chinese forms, not read from the page.

Pages: seven opened for the first version (the Kazakh-Dzungar Wars and Oirat Confederation pages are shared with the oirat-confederation dossier); four more on 2026-10-19 for the review repairs (Khanate of Kokand, Erdeni Batur, Turpan, Chinese expedition to Tibet 1720).

Review repairs, 2026-10-19 (ia-03-d-fixed): (a) 1680 counterpart yarkent-khanate -> eastern-moghulistan (reviewer, kept). (b) The 1677 gain of Dzungaria from khoshut-khanate is removed: it moved no land (Dzungaria is inside the 1658 keyframe); the Ochirtu victory stays as wars/2 with no zone, 1677 on the Dzungar page against 1678 on the Galdan page. (c) 1696 loss of Hami added (counterpart qing-dynasty, confidence 2) and the keyframes from 1696 corrected minus Hami. (d) 1723: the note no longer calls the Khujand-Samarkand-Andijan sweep 'raids'; the Kazakh-Dzungar Wars page does say 'occupying the Fergana Valley', but it gives no end and the Kokand page dates Dzungar invasions of Fergana to 1742 and 1745 only, so no Fergana occupation is drawn (confidence of the Syr Darya occupation lowered to 2). A Kokand-side note for the khanate-of-kokand dossier: Abd al-Karim Biy 'was eventually forced to make peace with the Dzungars' in 1745 and gave his son Baba Biy as hostage, and the Jungars 'forced Baba Biy on the Kokand throne' in 1752 (executed 1753): a possible short Dzungar vassal relation, not entered here. (e) The 1745 end of the Tashkent hold is contradicted by a 1734 Russian report on the Kazakh-Dzungar Wars page (cities 'abandoned because of the war with China'); confidence lowered to 2. (f) 1757 Tarim loss: counterpart is now the Aq Taghliq khojas, the Qing gain is 1759. Thin items tried: Turpan page silent on the defection year; Erdeni Batur page gives 1635 and 1646 raids, silent on Jetisu before 1658; Tibet 1720 page silent on the extent of the occupation. Disagreement: none with the reviewer; the 150 km radius first tried for Hami left a strip east of 93.9 E, so 220 km is used. fx-54 (3 Nov 2026): the December 1717 Tibet entry is an occupation_start and the 1720 entry an occupation_end, both with counterpart tibet (the page has an occupation under a military government, never an annexation).
